dependsOn: Stay iteration9, PR #534, protected deployment 37106203957 and matching public release manifest.
owner: Codex in James-approved Peninsula Insider task

baseline.source: Exact public Chromium at 390px after release 07c366d, with fresh localStorage and no pi-consent-v1 value.
baseline.observed: First-visit consent initially visible. Mobile menu opens and focuses Close navigation. One Escape closes the menu but also changes cookie-banner data-state from visible to hidden; pi-consent-v1 remains null. The prompt returns next visit, but disappears for the current visit without a choice.
baseline.reason: This is a reproduced AT/UX hard gate, not a fresh complete independent 23-criterion score.

finding: The document-level CookieBanner Escape listener hides a visible consent surface even when keyboard focus belongs to the mobile navigation dialog. Both handlers respond to the same Escape key.
hypothesis: Let consent respond to Escape only while focus is inside the consent surface. Then a menu Escape will close only navigation; consent Escape will still dismiss its own prompt without storing a choice, and a reopened dialog will restore focus to its opener.
boundedChange: Add a focus-ownership guard to CookieBanner onConsentKeydown. No consent storage shape, analytics choice, navigation, or booking behavior changes.
metric: On first visit at 390px, Escape from an open mobile menu closes the menu and preserves visible, unsaved consent. Escape from a focused consent control hides the prompt without storing a choice. Reopened preferences still focus Accept all, Escape restores the opening control, and Accept/Reject/Save persist the selected value. Build and independent browser QA pass; exact public manifest and browser confirm release.
rollback: Revert this one guarded listener change; no migration or data change.

validation.productionBuild: Final npm run build:search exited 0 on this exact source, including the existing content, rights, claim, SEO, link, schema and style gates; Astro output 1013 HTML files and Pagefind indexed 727 pages.
validation.settledBrowser: Local Chromium at 320 and 390px: fresh consent remained visible and unsaved through menu open and Escape, focus returned to Open navigation, and a second Escape with menu-button focus also left consent visible. Consent-focused Escape hid without storage and prompt returned on reload. Footer reopen focused Accept all; Escape returned focus to the footer trigger. Accept, Reject, and custom Save persisted the expected analytics values across reloads. No horizontal overflow.
validation.independentReview: Independent bounded release QA repeated local browser checks at 320 and 390px, including reopened consent with mobile drawer open: first Escape closed only the drawer, next consent-focused Escape closed only consent. It accepted release of this scoped guard. This is not a full 23-criterion grade.

hardGatesOpen: Exact public first-visit/menu Escape collision until published and verified
Full 23-criterion score remains unknown, with image rights, direct assistive technology, design and performance gates open
negativeFindings: Consent is not stored when the collision occurs, so analytics does not become opted in; the loss is the current-visit choice prompt.
CookieBanner already exempts an open Insider Note popup; the reproduced collision is the mobile navigation dialog.
nextAction: Publish the independently accepted guarded listener through protected CI, verify exact public SHA and mobile browser behavior, then continue open rubric gates.
